YES

The script drops exactly the 48 buffers via a full-match regex, casts exactly the 64 listed projection matrices to bfloat16 (float32 upcast then bfloat16, which equals a direct cast), upcasts every remaining tensor to float32, preserves names, enforces all four required checks with assertions before writing, and packs shards greedily at 268,435,456 bytes of tensor data with oversized tensors landing alone in their own shard, writing `model.safetensors.index.json` with a complete `weight_map`.
